newsitem.title: CANADA: Agrium sees strong '98 U.S. corn plantings.
newsitem.headline: Agrium sees strong '98 U.S. corn plantings.

text.p: Canadian fertilizer producer Agrium Inc said on Wednesday it did not believe this year's corn crop in the United States would be large enough to reduce the amount planted in 1998.

Agrium said positive fundamentals were expected to boost corn plantings and fertilizer consumption over the next several years, despite some industry fears that the 1997 crop will be so large it would create excess carry-over stocks.
"Below-average North American and world grain inventories will require more than one good crop year to restore stocks," the company said in its second-quarter results release.
Corn crops account for about 45 percent of farm fertilizer consumption. In the United States this year, corn was planted on 80.2 million acres, the most since 1985, Agrium said.
The company said elimination of U.S. government set-aside programs and a reduction in conservation reserve acreage were expected to increase the amount of land available for planting.
Agrium said urea prices in its market areas had resisted the large decline in the world market caused by oversupply due to a reduction in Chinese imports.
"Ammonia prices have actually increased compared to the same period last year. Most nitrogen products are currently in balance in North America," Agrium said.
Agrium said it expected higher potash prices this autumn and throughout 1998 because of strong domestic and offshore demand.

The completion of the company's potash mine expansion in Saskatchewan was expected to increase capacity by more than 15 percent overall with a 32 percent increase in premium product capacity, it said.
In Argentina, Agrium finalized talks to join Perez Companc SA and YPF SA in building a nitrogen complex in the South American country.

Under the deal, each firm will own a one-third stake in the plant, which was expected to cost about $450 million. Agrium currently owns 18 farm centers in Argentina. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
